human_tolerance.notes: The article says it is commonly found in suburbia, parks and gardens and that it readily comes to bird feeders, which is feeder-dependent garden bird behaviour.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Peak breeding season September to December; a cup nest is built in a tree and two to three pale blue eggs are laid.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Outside the breeding season the species is sociable and forms large flocks.

vocalizations.description: Very vocal: soft trilled 'pee', 'pree' or 'pirreee' contact notes kept up constantly, and a song of repeated long jerky phrases of sweet reedy notes varying in pitch, volume and tempo, usually opening with 'teee teee' or 'pirrup pirrup' and running on into a fast rambled jumble that may mimic other birds.

external.note: GBIF usageKey 7857709 from the species/match endpoint and iNaturalist taxon 472770 from the taxa endpoint; the Wikidata QID is the one the English article's taxobox links to.

conservation.note: The species article's taxobox records IUCN category Least Concern, credited there to BirdLife International.

range.note: 'South Africa, Botswana, Lesotho, Eswatini and marginally in Mozambique'. The article also records two interbreeding subspecies, capensis in the south-west and virens in the east, which is why both Western Cape and higher-rainfall climates are listed.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: A small perching passerine that hops through foliage and flies between perches; recorded from that description rather than stated as gaits.

traits.nest_type.note: 'It builds a cup nest in a tree'.

traits.perching.note: A perching, insessorial passerine with rounded wings and strong legs.

traits.mass_kg.note: AVONET Mass 11.1 g for Zosterops virens. AVONET's own Mass.Source field for this row reads DataFromSplit, that is the value was carried across when Zosterops pallidus was split off, rather than measured directly for Z. virens. It is the best openly licensed figure available and is flagged here rather than presented as a direct measurement.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Authored bracket of 9-13 g around the AVONET figure. No sourced range for this species was found; treat as an estimate.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Twice the AVONET Wing.Length of 58 mm, rounded to 0.116 m. AVONET does not give a wingspan directly.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Honest gap. Neither the species article, Wikidata nor GBIF gives a longevity figure for this species, and no openly licensed source with one was found. 5 years is an authored placeholder for a small passerine; it is not a sourced value.

traits.diet.note: 'Feeds mainly on insects, but also soft fleshy flowers, nectar, fruit and small grains'. The 0.5/0.2/0.2/0.1 split is authored from that ordering; the source gives no proportions.

traits.senses.note: Authored: diurnal passerine with coloured vision and modest olfaction.

traits.social.note: 'This is a sociable species forming large flocks outside the breeding season'. The upper bound of 40 is authored; the source gives no flock size.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Recorded as diurnal: an active daytime garden bird, with no nocturnal behaviour described.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement from a bird that 'readily comes to bird feeders' in suburban gardens.

habitat.use.note: AVONET classifies the habitat as Shrubland with an insessorial lifestyle; the article adds parks, gardens and wooded habitats. The 0.8 arboreal / 0.2 ground split is authored.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Authored: roosts in dense woody cover.

habitat.resources.note: Food tags follow the diet sentence in the article; perch, shrub_thicket and the cup nest follow 'cup nest in a tree' and the wooded habitats. Weights are authored.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: 'Commonly found in suburbia, parks and gardens' and 'readily comes to bird feeders' are both sourced; the Exploiter rating follows feeder use, and light_max is authored.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'Most populations are resident, but some perform minor seasonal movements' - no migration programme is described, so ActiveYearRound is recorded.

seasonal.phases.note: The September to December peak breeding season and the outside-breeding flocking behaviour are stated; the phase dates are authored from those.

seasonal.life_stages.note: 'The eggs hatch in 11-12 days, and fledging occurs in another 12-13 days'; rounded to 12 and 13. The scale of 0.85 is authored.

vocalizations.song.note: Both the trilled contact notes and the full song description, including the mimicked phrases of other birds, come from the Identification section.

look.note: Green upperparts, bright yellow throat and vent, and a conspicuous ring of white feathers round the eyes; the south-western subspecies Z. v. capensis has a grey breast and belly, which is the plumage in the Western Cape. Proportions are authored.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program: a small perching bird that glebs insects in trees and shrubs, is very vocal, and builds a cup nest in a tree between September and December. The program wants both a song and an alarm call, and the source documents only the contact calls and the song, so the same documented call serves both contexts.
